case_source: Appeal against the order of Mr. D.N. Chowdhury, Subordinate Judge of Zilla Noakhali, dated the 23rd of April, 1969 in Title Suit No. 150 of 1967.
full_judgment:
Sultan Hossain Khan, J. - This appeal arises out of an order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Noakhali rejecting an application for temporary injunction in a suit for declaration that auction sale of certain bazar was premature illegal and without jurisdiction and that certain tanks are retainable as khas under the provisions of section 20(2a) of the East Bengal State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.

2. Facts of the case, in short, are that the plaintiffs, who are the deities installed by the fore-fathers of the sebaites, instituted the suit against the Government and others for a declaration as follows:

(a) declaring that the auction sale of the Battapars Chowdhury Bazar in lzara lease for the remaining period of 1374 B.S. held on 4.10.67 A.D. in sairat case No. 12/1967-68 was premature, illegal, without jurisdiction and null and void.

(b) declaring that the two tanks covered by C.S. Plot 1628 of village Dattapara and C.S. Plot 13 of Village Darjipara, P.S. Lakshimpur are retainable khas land of the plaintiffs.

3. The plaintiffs have alleged that the land constituting the bazar known as Dattapara Chowdhury Bazar was owned by to debattars created by the predecessor of the Soebaites in favour of the deites long before. This bazar it has been alleged comprises a part of the suit lands. Plaintiffs have alleged that they had been in possession of the bazar but the Government without any possession had put the bazar to izara sale, and that the auction sale of the bazar was illegal and without jurisdiction. The plaintiffs have also prayed for an order of temporary injunction restraining the defendants from giving effect to the lease of the bazar for the remaining period of 1274 B.S.

4. The plaintiffs have further alleged that the two tanks as recorded in C.S. dag No. 1628 of Mouza Dattapara and dag No. 13 of Darjipara are retain able khas of the plaintiffs and that it should be so declared. The plaintiffs also prayed for an order of temporary injunction restraining the Government from leasing out the two tanks till the disposal of the suit.

5. Defendant No. 1 has opposed the application. They have alleged that the bazar in question has vested in Government under law and that the defendant are realising tolls from the bzar and that the bazar has been put to auction and that the izara had been taken by defendant No.6. With regard to the tanks the defendant has alleged that those have been used as a part of the bazar and as such these tanks have vested in the Government.

6. As regards the bazar it appears to us that neither of the parties could place anything before us as to the extent of the bazar as contemplated in section 20 (2a) of E.B.S.A.T. Act. For the purpose of the appeal we would say that any bazar which includes any land, building or hut therein cannot be retained by any rent-receiver or raiyat or tenant and as such the plaintiffs are not entitled to any injunction with respect to the bazar. With regard to the area or extent of the bazar as said earlier it should be left open to be determined in the trial. As regards the two tanks the plaintiffs have claimed them on the ground that these tanks are their khas land and as such they are entitled to retain them under section 20(2)(b). Defendants have alleged that those two tanks are part of the bazar and as such those could not be retained by the plaintiffs. Plaintiffs have alleged that these tanks are pot part of the bazar for they have been excavated long before the creation of the bazar in 1934. Undoubtedly these tanks are not natural formation and these have been excavated and the owners had been using the tanks for rearing and catching fish.

7. In our opinion tanks in which fish is reared are retainable in view of the provision of section 20(2a) of the Act. Although the plaintiffs have averred that people of the bazar and villagers use the water of the tanks, yet in our opinion it does not make the tanks part of the bazar. By use of water of the tanks no right whatsoever has been created in favour of the users.

In our view plaintiffs have succeeded in establishing a prima facie case that the tanks are retainable khas tanks of the plaintiffs.

Mr. J.R. Mudasir Hossain has submitted that compensation with respect to the lands of khatian No. 349 have been prepared and finally published and that compensation for acquisition of the suit lands have been received by the landlords.

8. We have perused the certified copy of the khatian placed before us. In this khatian we find that there are tanks and khas lands owned by the shebait on behalf of the deities. In the khatian there are tenanted lands as well. In our view compensation assessment roll must have been prepared with respect to re It receiving interests in the khatian. Nothing could be shown that the compensation assessment roll have been prepared and compensation has been received by the landlords with respect to the khas lands of the khatian.

9. In these views of the matter the order of the learned Subordinate Judge so far as it relates to the granting of temporary injunctions with respect to the bazar is affirmed and with respect to the two tanks are set aside. The defendants are restrained by way of an injunction from leasing out the suit tanks to anybody till the disposal of the suit.

10. In the result this appeal, is allowed in part. The judgment and order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge rejecting the application for injunction with regard to the bazar are affirmed and that relating to the suit tanks are set aside and the injunction prayed for with regard to the tanks is granted.

11. In the facts and circumstances of the case the parties are directed to maintain statuesque with regard to plot Nos. 6, 7 and 8 of Mouza Darjipara on which temple, Asram and the pathway are situated. In the facts of the case there will be no order as to cost in this appeal.

The learned Subordinate Judge is directed to dispose of the suit within six months from the date of the receipt of the records.

Mohammad Abdur Rouf J.-I agree.

End.
